key_insight: Machine learning can diagnose degradation mechanisms in simulated lead-free RbSn₀.₅Ge₀.₅I₃ solar cells, but accuracy depends strongly on training-data coverage.
engineering_relevance: The workflow supports post-fabrication fault diagnosis, while replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raises simulated efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, mainly through fill-factor gains.
method: Compare surrogate regression trained on factorial grids and Latin hypercube samples.
Use multi-label classification to identify six degradation mechanisms from temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit voltage.
evidence_signal: The diagnostic classifier achieves macro F₁ = 0.938 versus 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline; grid-trained regression falls from R² = 0.9997 on held-out grid points to 0.58 on independently sampled devices.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based, and the classifier does not generalize to degradation-mechanism combinations absent from training.
paper_title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
